docs.title: Overview
docs.text:
mkdocstrings-luau

A Luau handler for mkdocstrings.

Note

Currently, either Material for MkDocs or Zensical is supported

docs.title: Installation
docs.text: pip install mkdocstrings-luau

docs.title: Environment setup
docs.text:
Nothing easier!

Fork and clone the repository, then:

cd mkdocstrings-luau
make setup

Note

If it fails for some reason, you'll need to install uv manually.

You can install it with:

curl -LsSf https://astral.sh/uv/install.sh | sh

Now you can try running make setup again, or simply uv sync.

You now have the dependencies installed.

Run make help to see all the available actions!

docs.title: Tasks
docs.text:
The entry-point to run commands and tasks is the make Python script, located in the scripts directory. Try running make to show the available commands and tasks. The commands do not need the Python dependencies to be installed, while the tasks do. The cross-platform tasks are written in Python, thanks to duty.

If you work in VSCode, we provide an action to configure VSCode for the project.

docs.title: Development
docs.text:
As usual:

  1. create a new branch: git switch -c feature-or-bugfix-name
  2. edit the code and/or the documentation

Before committing:

  1. run make format to auto-format the code
  2. run make check to check everything (fix any warning)
  3. run make test to run the tests (fix any issue)
  4. if you updated the documentation or the project dependencies:
    1. run make docs
    2. go to http://localhost:8000 and check that everything looks good
  5. follow our commit message convention

If you are unsure about how to fix or ignore a warning, just let the continuous integration fail, and we will help you during review.

Don't bother updating the changelog, we will take care of this.

docs.title: Commit message convention
docs.text:
Commit messages must follow our convention based on the Angular style or the Karma convention:

<type>[(scope)]: Subject

[Body]

Subject and body must be valid Markdown. Subject must have proper casing (uppercase for first letter if it makes sense), but no dot at the end, and no punctuation in general.

Scope and body are optional. Type can be:

  • build: About packaging, building wheels, etc.
  • chore: About packaging or repo/files management.
  • ci: About Continuous Integration.
  • deps: Dependencies update.
  • docs: About documentation.
  • feat: New feature.
  • fix: Bug fix.
  • perf: About performance.
  • refactor: Changes that are not features or bug fixes.
  • style: A change in code style/format.
  • tests: About tests.

If you write a body, please add trailers at the end (for example issues and PR references, or co-authors), without relying on GitHub's flavored Markdown:

Body.

Issue #10: https://github.com/namespace/project/issues/10
Related to PR namespace/other-project#15: https://github.com/namespace/other-project/pull/15

These "trailers" must appear at the end of the body, without any blank lines between them. The trailer title can contain any character except colons :. We expect a full URI for each trailer, not just GitHub autolinks (for example, full GitHub URLs for commits and issues, not the hash or the #issue-number).

We do not enforce a line length on commit messages summary and body, but please avoid very long summaries, and very long lines in the body, unless they are part of code blocks that must not be wrapped.

docs.title: Pull requests guidelines
docs.text:
Link to any related issue in the Pull Request message.

During the review, we recommend using fixups:

# SHA is the SHA of the commit you want to fix
git commit --fixup=SHA

Once all the changes are approved, you can squash your commits:

git rebase -i --autosquash main

And force-push:

git push -f

If this seems all too complicated, you can push or force-push each new commit, and we will squash them ourselves if needed, before merging.

@classmethod
def coerce(cls, **data: Any) -> MutableMapping[str, Any]:
    """Coerce data."""
    if "inventories" in data:
        inventories = []
        for item in data["inventories"]:
            if isinstance(item, str):
                inventories.append(_Inventory(url=item))
            elif isinstance(item, _Inventory):
                inventories.append(item)
            else:
                inventories.append(_Inventory(**item))
        data["inventories"] = inventories
    return super().coerce(**data)

        base_dir: The base directory of the project.
        **kwargs: Arguments passed to the parent constructor.

    self.base_dir = base_dir

    self.global_options = config.options

def do_convert_markdown(
    self,
    text: str,
    heading_level: int,
    html_id: str = "",
    *,
    strip_paragraph: bool = False,
    autoref_hook: AutorefsHookInterface | None = None,
) -> Markup:
    """Render Markdown text; for use inside templates.

    Arguments:
        text: The text to convert.
        heading_level: The base heading level to start all Markdown headings from.
        html_id: The HTML id of the element that's considered the parent of this element.
        strip_paragraph: Whether to exclude the `<p>` tag from around the whole output.

    Returns:
        An HTML string.
    """
    global _markdown_conversion_layer  # noqa: PLW0603
    _markdown_conversion_layer += 1
    # Nested directives can replace self._md; finish and reset the converter that started this conversion.
    md = self.md
    treeprocessors = md.treeprocessors
    id_prefix = html_id and html_id + "--"
    treeprocessors[HeadingShiftingTreeprocessor.name].shift_by = heading_level  # ty:ignore[unresolved-attribute]
    treeprocessors[IdPrependingTreeprocessor.name].id_prefix = id_prefix  # ty:ignore[unresolved-attribute]
    treeprocessors[ParagraphStrippingTreeprocessor.name].strip = strip_paragraph  # ty:ignore[unresolved-attribute]
    if BacklinksTreeProcessor.name in treeprocessors:
        treeprocessors[BacklinksTreeProcessor.name].initial_id = html_id  # ty:ignore[unresolved-attribute]
    if autoref_hook and AutorefsInlineProcessor.name in md.inlinePatterns:
        md.inlinePatterns[AutorefsInlineProcessor.name].hook = autoref_hook  # ty:ignore[unresolved-attribute]

    try:
        with ExitStack() as stack:
            if id_prefix and "fenced_code_block" in md.preprocessors:
                fences = md.preprocessors["fenced_code_block"]
                if isinstance(fences, SuperFencesBlockPreprocessor):
                    # SuperFences caches Highlight settings, so prefix its active values before preprocessing.
                    fences.get_hl_settings()
                    stack.enter_context(_prepend_code_ids(fences, id_prefix))
            return Markup(md.convert(text))
    finally:
        treeprocessors[HeadingShiftingTreeprocessor.name].shift_by = 0  # ty:ignore[unresolved-attribute]
        treeprocessors[IdPrependingTreeprocessor.name].id_prefix = ""  # ty:ignore[unresolved-attribute]
        treeprocessors[ParagraphStrippingTreeprocessor.name].strip = False  # ty:ignore[unresolved-attribute]
        if BacklinksTreeProcessor.name in treeprocessors:
            treeprocessors[BacklinksTreeProcessor.name].initial_id = None  # ty:ignore[unresolved-attribute]
        if AutorefsInlineProcessor.name in md.inlinePatterns:
            md.inlinePatterns[AutorefsInlineProcessor.name].hook = None  # ty:ignore[unresolved-attribute]
        md.reset()
        _markdown_conversion_layer -= 1

def do_heading(
    self,
    content: Markup,
    heading_level: int,
    *,
    role: str | None = None,
    hidden: bool = False,
    toc_label: str | None = None,
    skip_inventory: bool = False,
    **attributes: str,
) -> Markup:
    """Render an HTML heading and register it for the table of contents. For use inside templates.

    Arguments:
        content: The HTML within the heading.
        heading_level: The level of heading (e.g. 3 -> `h3`).
        role: An optional role for the object bound to this heading.
        hidden: If True, only register it for the table of contents, don't render anything.
        toc_label: The title to use in the table of contents ('data-toc-label' attribute).
        skip_inventory: Flag element to not be registered in the inventory (by setting a `data-skip-inventory` attribute).
        **attributes: Any extra HTML attributes of the heading.

    Returns:
        An HTML string.
    """
    # Produce a heading element that will be used later, in `AutoDocProcessor.run`, to:
    # - register it in the ToC: right now we're in the inner Markdown conversion layer,
    #   so we have to bubble up the information to the outer Markdown conversion layer,
    #   for the ToC extension to pick it up.
    # - register it in autorefs: right now we don't know what page is being rendered,
    #   so we bubble up the information again to where autorefs knows the page,
    #   and can correctly register the heading anchor (id) to its full URL.
    # - register it in the objects inventory: same as for autorefs,
    #   we don't know the page here, or the handler (and its domain),
    #   so we bubble up the information to where the mkdocstrings extension knows that.
    el = Element(f"h{heading_level}", attributes)
    if toc_label is None:
        toc_label = content.unescape() if isinstance(content, Markup) else content
    el.set("data-toc-label", toc_label)
    if skip_inventory:
        el.set("data-skip-inventory", "true")
    if role:
        el.set("data-role", role)
    if content:
        el.text = str(content).strip()
    self._headings.append(el)

    if hidden:
        return Markup('<a id="{0}"></a>').format(attributes["id"])

    # Now produce the actual HTML to be rendered. The goal is to wrap the HTML content into a heading.
    # Start with a heading that has just attributes (no text), and add a placeholder into it.
    el = Element(f"h{heading_level}", attributes)
    el.append(Element("mkdocstrings-placeholder"))
    # Tell the inner 'toc' extension to make its additions if configured so.
    toc = cast("TocTreeprocessor", self.md.treeprocessors["toc"])
    if toc.use_anchors:
        toc.add_anchor(el, attributes["id"])
    if toc.use_permalinks:
        toc.add_permalink(el, attributes["id"])

    # The content we received is HTML, so it can't just be inserted into the tree. We had marked the middle
    # of the heading with a placeholder that can never occur (text can't directly contain angle brackets).
    # Now this HTML wrapper can be "filled" by replacing the placeholder.
    html_with_placeholder = tostring(el, encoding="unicode")
    assert (  # noqa: S101
        html_with_placeholder.count("<mkdocstrings-placeholder />") == 1
    ), f"Bug in mkdocstrings: failed to replace in {html_with_placeholder!r}"
    html = html_with_placeholder.replace("<mkdocstrings-placeholder />", content)
    return Markup(html)

def get_aliases(self, identifier: str) -> tuple[str, ...]:
    """Get aliases for a given identifier.

    Parameters:
        identifier: Heading id, which is the object's canonical path.

    Returns:
        The canonical path and, for methods, the colon spelling `Class:method`.
    """
    item = self._collected.get(identifier)
    if item is None and self._library is not None:
        try:
            item = self._library.resolve(identifier)
        except KeyError:
            return ()
    if item is None:
        return ()
    aliases = [item.path]
    if isinstance(item, Function) and item.kind == "method" and item.parent is not None:
        aliases.append(f"{item.parent.name}:{item.name}")
    return tuple(dict.fromkeys(aliases))

def get_templates_dir(self, handler: str | None = None) -> Path:
    """Return the path to the handler's templates directory.

    Override to customize how the templates directory is found.

    Arguments:
        handler: The name of the handler to get the templates directory of.

    Raises:
        ModuleNotFoundError: When no such handler is installed.
        FileNotFoundError: When the templates directory cannot be found.

    Returns:
        The templates directory path.
    """
    handler = handler or self.name
    try:
        import mkdocstrings_handlers  # noqa: PLC0415
    except ModuleNotFoundError as error:
        raise ModuleNotFoundError(f"Handler '{handler}' not found, is it installed?") from error

    for path in mkdocstrings_handlers.__path__:
        theme_path = Path(path, handler, "templates")
        if theme_path.exists():
            return theme_path

    raise FileNotFoundError(f"Can't find 'templates' folder for handler '{handler}'")

def load_inventory(
    in_file: BinaryIO,
    url: str,
    base_url: str | None = None,
    domains: list[str] | None = None,
    **kwargs: Any,  # noqa: ARG004
) -> Iterator[tuple[str, str]]:
    """Yield items and their URLs from an inventory file streamed from `in_file`.

    Parameters:
        in_file: The binary file-like object to read the inventory from.
        url: The URL that this file is being streamed from (used to guess `base_url`).
        base_url: The URL that this inventory's sub-paths are relative to.
        domains: Domains to keep. Defaults to `luau`.
        **kwargs: Ignore additional arguments passed from the config.

    Yields:
        Tuples of (item identifier, item URL).
    """
    domains = domains or ["luau"]
    if base_url is None:
        base_url = posixpath.dirname(url)
    for item in Inventory.parse_sphinx(in_file, domain_filter=domains).values():
        yield item.name, posixpath.join(base_url, item.uri)

def render(self, data: CollectorItem, options: LuauOptions, *, locale: str | None = None) -> str:  # noqa: ARG002
    """Render a template using provided data and configuration options.

    Parameters:
        data: Collected Luau object.
        options: Combined rendering options.
        locale: Unused. Templates are English.

    Returns:
        Rendered HTML.
    """
    try:
        template_name, variable = _TEMPLATES[data.kind]
    except KeyError as error:
        raise CollectionError(f"Don't know how to render {data.kind!r}") from error
    context: dict[str, Any] = {
        "config": options,
        variable: data,
        "heading_level": options.heading_level,
        "root": True,
    }
    if isinstance(data, Class):
        context["members"] = _select_members(data, options)
    if isinstance(data, Property) and _is_event(data, options.event_types):
        context["member_symbol"] = "event"
    return self.env.get_template(template_name).render(**context)

@classmethod
def coerce(cls, **data: Any) -> MutableMapping[str, Any]:
    """Coerce data."""
    if "members" in data:
        members = data["members"]
        if members is True or members is None:
            data["members"] = None
        elif members is False:
            data["members"] = []
        elif isinstance(members, str):
            data["members"] = [members]
    if "filters" in data and isinstance(data["filters"], str):
        data["filters"] = [data["filters"]]
    if "event_types" in data and isinstance(data["event_types"], str):
        data["event_types"] = [data["event_types"]]
    order = data.get("members_order", "source")
    if order not in {"alphabetical", "source"}:
        raise ValueError(f"members_order must be 'alphabetical' or 'source', not {order!r}")
    style = data.get("docstring_section_style", "table")
    if style not in {"table", "list"}:
        raise ValueError(f"docstring_section_style must be 'table' or 'list', not {style!r}")
    return data

docs.title: Usage
docs.text: Document Luau with Moonwave comments, then let mkdocstrings render them.

docs.title: Install
docs.text:
pip install mkdocstrings-luau

You also need the Moonwave extractor when the handler runs it during the build. moonwave-extractor is a Rust binary. If you would rather not ship it in CI, run it yourself and point the handler at the JSON file.

docs.title: Configure MkDocs
docs.text:
mkdocs.yml
site_name: My Luau library
theme:
  name: material

plugins:
- search
- autorefs
- mkdocstrings:
    handlers:
      luau:
        extractor: moonwave-extractor
        paths:
        - src
        options:
          show_source: true
          show_symbol_type_heading: true
          signature_crossrefs: true

paths are files or directories of .lua / .luau sources. They are passed to moonwave-extractor extract. Set json instead when the JSON already exists:

mkdocs.yml
plugins:
- mkdocstrings:
    handlers:
      luau:
        json: docs/api.json

json wins when both are set. Paths inside the JSON are relative to base (the extractor's --base), which defaults to the directory that contains mkdocs.yml.

docs.title: Document a class
docs.text:
Moonwave comments use --[=[ blocks (or --- lines). The extractor groups functions, properties, and types under a class.

src/Vector3.luau
--[=[
    @class Vector3

    A three-component vector. Create one with [Vector3.new].
]=]
local Vector3 = {}

--[=[
    @param x number -- X component
    @param y number -- Y component
    @param z? number -- Optional Z
    @return Vector3
]=]
function Vector3.new(x: number, y: number, z: number?): Vector3
    return setmetatable({ X = x, Y = y, Z = z or 0 }, Vector3)
end

--[=[
    @param other Vector3 -- The other vector
    @return number
]=]
function Vector3:dot(other: Vector3): number
    return self.X * other.X + self.Y * other.Y + (self.Z or 0) * (other.Z or 0)
end

In a Markdown page, with handler: luau selected globally or on the directive:

::: Vector3

::: Vector3.dot

::: Vector3:dot

Class.member is the canonical identifier. Methods can also be written Class:method. [Vector3.new] inside a Moonwave description becomes a cross-reference when that object is rendered. @external Promise https://... links that type name to the URL.

See the configuration reference for every option.

docs.title: Not handled yet
docs.text:
Moonwave's extractor does the parsing. This handler does not read Luau itself, and it does not invent features Moonwave's JSON does not carry:

  • @link and @enum are unimplemented in Moonwave, so they never appear in the JSON.
  • There is no class inheritance. @class does not record a base class.
  • Roblox engine types (such as Instance or Player) are not linked unless you document them or declare them with @external.
  • Parameters have no default values. Returns have a type and a description, not a name.
  • Source excerpts are the declaration line for properties and types, and the following block for functions, when the file from source.path can be read. The JSON itself only includes the path and line.
  • Templates are written for the Material theme. MkDocs and Read the Docs themes fall back to those templates.
  • If the same class is extracted from more than one path, members are concatenated. Two members with the same name are an error.

docs.title: Customization
docs.text: It is possible to customize the output of the generated documentation with CSS and/or by overriding templates.

docs.title: CSS classes
docs.text:
Our templates add CSS classes to many HTML elements to make it possible for users to customize the resulting look and feel.

To add CSS rules and style mkdocstrings' output, put them in a CSS file in your docs folder, for example in docs/css/mkdocstrings.css, and reference this file in MkDocs' extra_css configuration option:

mkdocs.yml
extra_css:
- css/mkdocstrings.css

Example:

docs/css/mkdocstrings.css
.doc-section-title {
  font-weight: bold;
}

docs.title: Colors
docs.text:
You can customize the colors of the symbol types (see show_symbol_type_heading and show_symbol_type_toc) by overriding the values of our CSS variables, for example:

docs/css/mkdocstrings.css
[data-md-color-scheme="default"] {
  --doc-symbol-class-fg-color: #d1b619;

  --doc-symbol-class-bg-color: #d1b6191a;
}

[data-md-color-scheme="slate"] {
  --doc-symbol-class-fg-color: #46c2cb;

  --doc-symbol-class-bg-color: #46c2cb1a;
}

The [data-md-color-scheme="*"] selectors work with the [Material for MkDocs] theme. If you are using another theme, adapt the selectors to this theme if it supports light and dark themes, otherwise just override the variables at root level:

docs/css/mkdocstrings.css
:root {
  --doc-symbol-class-fg-color: #d1b619;

  --doc-symbol-class-bg-color: #d1b6191a;
}

Preview

Try cycling through the themes to see the colors for each theme:

docs.title: Names
docs.text:
You can also change the actual symbol names. For example, to use single letters instead of truncated types:

docs/css/mkdocstrings.css
.doc-symbol-class::after {
  content: "C";
}

docs.title: Templates
docs.text:
Templates are organized into the following tree:

📁 theme/
├──  children.html.jinja
├──  class.html.jinja
├──  deprecated.html.jinja
├──  description.html.jinja
├──  errors.html.jinja
├──  fields.html.jinja
├──  function.html.jinja
├──  labels.html.jinja
├──  parameters.html.jinja
├──  property.html.jinja
├──  returns.html.jinja
├──  source.html.jinja
├──  summary.html.jinja
└──  type.html.jinja

See them in the repository. See the general mkdocstrings documentation to learn how to override them: https://mkdocstrings.github.io/theming/#templates.

Each one of these templates extends a base version in theme/_base. Example:

theme/class.html.jinja
{% extends "_base/class.html.jinja" %}

Some of these templates define Jinja blocks. allowing to customize only parts of a template without having to fully copy-paste it into your project:

templates/theme/class.html.jinja
{% extends "_base/class.html.jinja" %}
{% block contents scoped %}
  {{ block.super }}
  Additional contents
{% endblock contents %}

docs.title: Global/local options
docs.text:
The other options can be used both globally and locally, under the options key. For example, globally:

mkdocs.yml
plugins:
- mkdocstrings:
    handlers:
      python:
        options:
          do_something: true

...and locally, overriding the global configuration:

docs/some_page.md
::: package.module.class
    options:
      do_something: false

These options affect how the documentation is collected from sources and rendered. See the following tables summarizing the options, and get more details for each option in the following pages:

  • Sources: where Moonwave JSON comes from, and remote inventories
  • General options: signatures, labels, source, and section style
  • Headings options: options related to headings and the table of contents (or sidebar, depending on the theme used)
  • Members options: which class members are rendered, and in what order

docs.title: extra
docs.text:
• Type dict {}

The extra option lets you inject additional variables into the Jinja context used when rendering templates. You can then use this extra context in your overridden templates.

Local extra options will be merged into the global extra option:

in mkdocs.yml (global configuration)
plugins:
- mkdocstrings:
    handlers:
      luau:
        options:
          extra:
            hello: world
in docs/some_page.md (local configuration)
::: your_package.your_module.your_func
    options:
      extra:
        foo: bar

...will inject both hello and foo into the Jinja context when rendering your_package.your_module.your_func.

docs.title: show_source
docs.text:
• Type bool True

Show the path:line Moonwave recorded. When that file exists under base, the declaration is included: one line for properties and types, and the following block for functions.

docs.title: show_signature
docs.text:
• Type bool True

Show a Luau signature. Methods use :, static functions use ., and a parameter documented as name? is rendered as an optional type.

docs.title: separate_signature
docs.text:
• Type bool False

Put the signature under the heading instead of inside it. The heading then shows the object name.

docs.title: signature_crossrefs
docs.text:
• Type bool True

Link types in parameter, return, error, and field tables, and on the type line under each property. A type that names a documented object points at that object. A type declared with @external points at that URL, including builtins such as boolean and string when you declare them. Builtins without an @external entry stay as plain type text.

docs.title: show_labels
docs.text:
• Type bool True

Show labels next to the heading: deprecated, private, unreleased, ignored, realms (client, server, plugin), custom @tag values, static, yields, and readonly.

docs.title: docstring_section_style
docs.text:
• Type str "table"

Render parameters, returns, errors, and fields as a table or a list.

Descriptions are Markdown, rendered with the same Markdown extensions as the rest of the site. [Class.member] and [Class:method] are Moonwave shortcut links and become cross-references. Class.member is also the anchor registered for autorefs.

docs.title: heading
docs.text:
• Type str ""

A custom string to use as the heading of the root object (i.e. the object specified directly after the identifier :::). This will override the default heading generated by the plugin. See also the toc_label option.

Not advised to be used as a global configuration option

This option is not advised to be used as a global configuration option, as it will override the default heading for all objects. It is recommended to use it only in specific cases where you want to override the heading for a specific object.

in docs/some_page.md (local configuration)
::: path.to.module
    options:
      heading: "My fancy module"

docs.title: heading_level
docs.text:
• Type int 2

The initial heading level to use.

When injecting documentation for an object, the object itself and its members are rendered. For each layer of objects, we increase the heading level by 1.

The initial heading level will be used for the first layer. If you set it to 3, then headings will start with <h3>.

plugins:

    handlers:
      luau:
        options:
          heading_level: 2

docs.title: toc_label
docs.text:
• Type str ""

A custom string to use as the label in the Table of Contents for the root object (i.e. the one specified directly after the identifier :::). This will override the default label generated by the plugin. See also the heading option.

Not advised to be used as a global configuration option

This option is not advised to be used as a global configuration option, as it will override the default label for all objects. It is recommended to use it only in specific cases where you want to override the label for a specific object.

Use with/without heading

If you use this option without specifying a custom heading, the default heading will be used in the page, but the label in the Table of Contents will be the one you specified. By providing both an option for heading and toc_label, we leave the customization entirely up to you.

in docs/some_page.md (local configuration)
::: path.to.module
    options:
      heading: "My fancy module"
      toc_label: "My fancy module"

docs.title: show_root_heading
docs.text:
• Type bool True

Show a heading for the object named by :::. Set it to false when the page title already names that object. The anchor is still emitted when show_root_toc_entry is true.

docs.title: show_root_toc_entry
docs.text:
• Type bool True

When the root heading is hidden, still add the object to the table of contents and register its anchor.

docs.title: show_root_full_path
docs.text:
• Type bool False

Show the full identifier (Vector3.dot) in the root heading instead of the short name.

docs.title: show_root_members_full_path
docs.text:
• Type bool False

Show full identifiers for members rendered under the root object.

docs.title: show_object_full_path
docs.text:
• Type bool False

Show full identifiers for nested objects. Also applies to root members when show_root_members_full_path is false.

docs.title: Members options
docs.text: These options control which members of a class are rendered. Asking for a member directly, as in ::: Vector3.Y, still collects that member even when it would be hidden on the class page.

docs.title: show_category_heading
docs.text:
• Type bool True

Show a heading for each non-empty group: Properties, Events, Types, Functions, and Methods.

docs.title: event_types
docs.text:
• Type liststr ["BindableEvent", "RBXScriptSignal", "Signal"]

Moonwave does not have an @event tag. Properties are rendered under Events when their type contains one of these names, or when the property has a custom @tag event. An empty list turns off the type match; @tag event still opens an Events section.

mkdocs.yml
plugins:
- mkdocstrings:
    handlers:
      luau:
        options:
          event_types:
          - BindableEvent
          - RBXScriptSignal

docs.title: summary
docs.text:
• Type bool True

Show a summary table of the visible members before their full documentation.

docs.title: show_private
docs.text:
• Type bool False

Include members marked with Moonwave's @private tag.

docs.title: show_unreleased
docs.text:
• Type bool False

Include members marked with @unreleased.

docs.title: show_ignored
docs.text:
• Type bool False

Include members marked with @ignore.

docs.title: members
docs.text:
• Type liststr | None None

Names of members to render. None or true means every member that passes the visibility flags and filters. false or [] renders none. A string is treated as a one-item list.

::: Vector3
    options:
      members:
      - new
      - dot

docs.title: filters
docs.text:
• Type liststr []

Regular expressions matched against member names. A pattern prefixed with ! excludes matches. Later patterns win, which is the same rule the Python handler uses.

mkdocs.yml
plugins:
- mkdocstrings:
    handlers:
      luau:
        options:
          filters:
          - "!^_"

docs.title: members_order
docs.text:
• Type str "source"

source keeps Moonwave's source order (line number, then name). alphabetical sorts by name.

docs.title: Sources
docs.text: These settings live on the handler itself, next to options, because they describe where the documentation comes from.

docs.title: extractor
docs.text:
• Type str "moonwave-extractor"

Path or command name of the Moonwave extractor binary. The handler runs extractor extract <path> --base <base> for each entry in paths.

mkdocs.yml
plugins:
- mkdocstrings:
    handlers:
      luau:
        extractor: moonwave-extractor

docs.title: paths
docs.text:
• Type liststr []

Luau files or directories to extract. Directories are walked for .lua and .luau files by Moonwave. Relative paths are resolved from the directory that contains mkdocs.yml.

Ignored when json is set.

docs.title: json
docs.text:
• Type str ""

Path to a JSON file already produced by moonwave-extractor. When this is non-empty, the extractor is not run. The file must be an array of class objects (a single class object is accepted too).

mkdocs.yml
plugins:
- mkdocstrings:
    handlers:
      luau:
        json: docs/api.json

docs.title: base
docs.text:
• Type str ""

Directory passed as --base. Source paths in the JSON are relative to it, and the handler reads those files from there when show_source can show the declaration. An empty value means the directory that contains mkdocs.yml.

docs.title: inventories
docs.text:
• Type list []

Sphinx objects.inv files to download so cross-references can point at objects rendered by another site. Each entry is a URL, or a mapping with url, optional base_url, and optional domains (default ["luau"]).

mkdocs.yml
plugins:
- mkdocstrings:
    handlers:
      luau:
        inventories:
        - https://example.com/objects.inv
        - url: https://example.com/objects.inv
          base_url: https://example.com/
          domains: [luau]

Objects rendered by this handler are written to this site's own inventory with domain luau and roles class, function, method, property, and type. Method headings also register the Class:method alias.
